messages:
jordan-customer: Hey team — our CI runners in the customer's VPC started failing during onboarding. `pip install` hangs and the private installer can't pull model shards. We see timeouts and TLS/SNI errors. Can you share a minimal egress allowlist for: CI runners, the on-prem installer, model registry pulls, telemetry, and auth/KMS calls?

lucy-support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a short repro (curl) and one of the failing job logs? Also tell us if you're behind a corporate proxy / TLS interception.

jordan-customer: here's the easiest repro from a runner inside their VPC:
```
$ curl -vI https://model-registry.redwood-inference.com
* Trying 10.1.2.45...
* Connected to 10.1.2.45 (10.1.2.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* SSL: certificate subject name 'model-registry.redwood-inference.com' does not match host '10.1.2.45'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'model-registry.redwood-inference.com' does not match host '10.1.2.45'
```
We also see repeated timeouts when the installer tries to curl `https://installs.redwood-inference.com/bootstrap.sh` and when the runtime attempts to fetch shards from `shards-prod-us-west-1.models.redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com`.

lucy-support: that cert mismatch strongly suggests SNI is being stripped or the firewall is doing IP-based routing (split-horizon). Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm outbound TCP 443 is allowed to hostnames below? 2) do you have TLS MITM / proxy terminating TLS? If so we need allowlist exceptions (passthrough) for these hosts.

khalid-infra: minimal allowlist we recommend for CI + installer + model pulls (allow outbound TCP 443; allow UDP 53 for DNS). Prefer FQDN-based rules where possible: 
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- installs.redwood-inference.com
- model-registry.redwood-inference.com
- shards-prod-*.models.redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com (S3 hostnames for shard downloads)
- artifacts.redwood-inference.com (internal artifactory/cdn)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS, for metrics/health pings)
- auth.redwood-inference.com (token exchange)
- kms.*.amazonaws.com (for KMS-backed key ops)
- ocsp.digicert.com
- crl.globalsign.net
- *.cloudfront.net (CDN for some artifacts)
Also allow outbound TCP 80 for redirects during bootstrap. If you must use IP rules, use cloud provider published ranges (e.g., AWS ip-ranges.json) and only allow the prefixes for the regions you use.

infra-bot: deploy-job-4872 FAILED: downloader timed out after 120s (see job logs).

oncall-jen: additional checklist items:
- Ensure TLS passthrough for the above hosts (no corporate TLS interception) — SNI must be preserved.
- If using transparent proxy, allow SNI-based routing or carve out exceptions for these FQDNs.
- Allow DNS resolution to public resolvers (UDP/53) or whitelist the resolver IPs used by your VPC.
- Allow access to OCSP/CRL endpoints so certificate validation doesn't hang.

jordan-customer: thanks. One more: the firewall team wants specific IPs for `model-registry.redwood-inference.com` and the shard S3 buckets so they can add precise CIDRs. Can you give guidance on which IP ranges to add?

khalid-infra: for exact IPs we recommend either: 1) allow FQDNs (preferred), or 2) pull the latest AWS IP ranges and allow the S3/CloudFront prefixes for the regions used by your account — AWS publishes them here: https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json. Example approach: allow CloudFront (global) prefixes plus the S3 prefixes for the region (e.g., us-west-1) that host our shards. We can't publish static single-IP addresses because CDNs and cloud infra change.

lucy-support: to validate after changes, run these two quick checks from a runner inside the VPC: 
```
# verify SNI + cert chain
curl -vI https://model-registry.redwood-inference.com
# check download from an S3 shard (replace with a known shard path)
curl -vO https://shards-prod-us-west-1.models.redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/abc1234/model.pt
```
If both succeed (200/HEAD and no certificate errors), CI and installer should be unblocked.

jordan-customer: applying rules now. I'll confirm once firewall accepts FQDN-based rules or we add the AWS prefixes. Appreciate the checklist — will update here shortly. :thumbsup:
